headline: Kai, Brazil chooses between Lula and a Bolsonaro today, and Wednesday stacks the Fed's $116-oil decision on top of Microsoft and Alphabet earnings.
subline: Hold odds sit near 91 percent, bitcoin starts the week at $80,853 under its 50-day line, and the Gulf keeps crude bid at a six-month high.
asof: Sunday edition · markets closed · stocks, gold and oil are Friday's close · bitcoin as of 6:30 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: The week's ledger: S&P −0.5%, Russell +2%
items.sentence: AP's weekly ledger puts the S&P 500 at 7,623.68 (−0.5 percent for the week, +11.4 percent this year), the Dow at 52,215.16, the Nasdaq at 25,955.34, and the Russell 2000 up 2 percent on the week.

items.title: The Fed convenes Tuesday; hold odds near 91%
items.sentence: TradingKey notes CME FedWatch prices a 90.6 percent hold for Wednesday's 2 pm statement — the first decision since September's hike to 3.75–4.00 percent — with no dot plot this round and Q3 GDP plus September PCE due Thursday.

items.title: Alphabet and Microsoft Wednesday, Amazon Thursday
items.sentence: Kiplinger's calendar has Alphabet ($3.00 a share expected on $127.9 billion of revenue) and Microsoft ($4.71) Wednesday after the close, Amazon ($1.96) and Intel Thursday, and Exxon and Chevron Friday morning.

items.title: Oil desks map $108 to $120 for Fed week
items.sentence: FinanceFeeds' week-ahead pegs Brent's bull case at $120 on resumed US strikes and its bear case at $108 on a pre-midterm ceasefire signal, after Washington authorized an emergency SPR exchange of up to 400,000 barrels.

items.title: Bitcoin opens Fed week at $80,853
items.sentence: CryptoTicker has bitcoin at $80,853 Sunday morning, flat over 24 hours and still below the 50-day line at $81,807 it lost Friday, with $909.7 million of two-week ETF outflows and an $11.1 billion options expiry this Friday.

items.title: Brazil picks between Lula and a Bolsonaro today
items.sentence: Per The Rio Times, Brazilians vote today in a presidential runoff between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the convicted former president.

items.title: Mines near Hormuz as US weighs new strikes
items.sentence: Gulf News reports Houthi missiles targeted Riyadh, tankers were hit and mines appeared near the Strait of Hormuz, as Washington prepares possible strikes on Iran.

items.title: Michigan's Senate race pulls in Trump and Obama
items.sentence: inkl's Sunday bulletin has Trump campaigning for Republican Mike Rogers while Obama backs Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, nine days before the November 3 midterms.

items.title: NATO rehearses drone-war defense over Germany
items.sentence: RFI reports, via the same bulletin, that French paratroopers joined British forces in a major airborne exercise testing NATO's defenses against drone and electronic-warfare threats.

items.title: Banks wall off accounts from unvetted AI agents
items.sentence: Axios reports unvetted third-party AI agents have been accessing US bank accounts, prompting major banks to move to restrict their access.

items.title: UAE investors lead OpenAI's $30 billion round
items.sentence: CNBC reports OpenAI is nearing a funding round of up to $30 billion, led by UAE investors, that would value the company at $1.25 trillion.

items.title: Jack Clark takes the singularity to the IMF
items.sentence: How Machines Think's weekly roundup has Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark telling IMF and World Bank meetings that benchmark leaps leave policymakers 'a small number of years' to set limits.

items.title: Mega-cap earnings double as the AI referendum
items.sentence: KuCoin News calls this week's Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon reports an earnings test for US tech stocks still nursing October's AI-led selloff.
